chunks: Enhancement vs depletion mode MOSFET. The question: What is the difference between enhancement-mode and depletion mode?
The two modes differ in whether a channel already exists with zero gate voltage. An enhancement-mode MOSFET has no channel until you apply a gate voltage, so it starts off.
A depletion-mode MOSFET has a channel built in during manufacturing, so it starts on. Almost every MOSFET you buy is enhancement mode.
Picture two doors. The enhancement door is normally locked, and you have to push a button to open it.
The depletion door is normally open, and you have to push a button to close it. Many designs prefer the locked door, because if power is lost the circuit fails safely off.
The analogy fails on one point: for an N-channel depletion door, the button is a negative gate voltage.
The only structural difference is the thin implanted n-layer (shaded strip under the gate in the right-hand device).
It gives the depletion device a conducting path at zero gate bias; the enhancement device must have the gate create it.
Channel: the thin conducting layer between source and drain. Threshold voltage ( V t ): the gate voltage where the device changes state. Enhancement mode: normally off.
For N-channel, V t is positive. Depletion mode: normally on. For N-channel, V t is negative. Normally off / normally on: the state with the gate at 0 volts.
Say an N-channel enhancement MOSFET has V t equals plus 1 volts. At V GS equals 0 it is off, and at V GS equals 2 volts it is on.
Now say an N-channel depletion MOSFET has V t equals -2 volts. At V GS equals 0 it is already on, and you must pull the gate below -2 volts, say to -3 volts, to turn it off.
Use enhancement parts as switches. Use depletion parts where something must work before everything else powers up. That is the whole idea.
"The mode tells you whether a channel exists at zero gate voltage.
Enhancement mode has no channel at V GS equals 0 , so it's normally off and you apply a gate voltage above V t to create one. That's nearly every MOSFET.
Depletion mode has a channel implanted at fabrication, so it conducts at zero gate voltage and you apply a gate voltage of the opposite polarity to cut it off.
For an N-channel that means a negative threshold. The equations are identical, just with a negative V t , and depletion parts are used for start-up circuits and current sources."
Quick check. Which describes an N-channel depletion-mode MOSFET?
